newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia June quarter CPI falls 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia June quarter CPI falls 0.2 pct.

text.p: The Australian consumer price index (CPI) fell 0.2 percent in the June quarter for an annual inflation rate of 0.3 percent, the Bureau of Statistics said.
The Treasury's measure of underlying inflation rose 0.3 percent in the June quarter to stand at 1.7 percent for the year, the lowest annual underlying inflation rate since the series started in 1971.
In the March quarter, the CPI rose 0.2 percent for an annual inflation rate of 1.3 percent, while underlying inflation rose 0.4 percent for an annual 2.1 percent.
Main features (pct) June qtr/March qtr June qtr/June qtr
Most analysts had expected the June quarter CPI to fall by 0.1 percent for an annual rate of 0.5 percent, and underlying inflation to rise 0.4 percent for an annual 1.7 percent.
The fall in the CPI was the first since the June quarter of 1992 and the lowest annual rise since the December quarter 1992.

The bureau said contributing most to the decrease in the quarter CPI were falls in mortgage interest charges, which were down 9.6 percent, the price of motor vehicles, automotive fuel and domestic holiday travel and accommodation.
Partially offsetting these were increases the cost of hospital and medical services and the price of furniture.
The CPI excluding housing rose 0.2 percent in the June quarter for an annual 2.0 percent.
